open_points.subject: A28 elapsed-clock use by the transport guard
open_points.text: Every HTTP request first passes the transport guard of A25 (one middleware installed by the runtime): trusted host, body bound, viewer-entry rate limit, viewer sign-out origin, security and `no-store` headers, one redacted log line.
open_points.question: Which named clock-source capability does the transport guard call for the viewer-entry rate-limit reading, and which component owns making exactly one such call per viewer-entry request?
options: The transport guard directly calls a named monotonic-reading capability once per viewer-entry request
A separate rate-limiter operation calls the monotonic capability and the transport guard delegates to it
The runtime reads the elapsed clock and passes a value into the transport guard
open_points.default_guess: Make the transport guard's viewer-entry limiter call a named clock-source monotonic capability exactly once per viewer-entry request.

set_aside.subject: A28 wall-clock source integration across State 4 flows
set_aside.text: one clock source is the only reader of both; every other part of the portal obtains time from it and never reads a host clock itself
set_aside.question: What named module capability supplies the single wall-clock reading to each State 4 operation that creates timestamps, derives expiries, checks expiries, or revokes records, and does the owning use case call it or receive its instant from its caller?
options: Each owning use case calls a named wall-clock capability once and reuses the returned instant
The route or another coordinator reads the clock once and passes the instant to the use case
Each affected module receives an injected clock object but no shared capability is named
set_aside.default_guess: Add a clock-source module with a wall-reading capability and have each owning use case call it once per operation.
